ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and registered agents against United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List, AUSTRAC-style domestic financial intelligence watchlists, and VFSC adverse media and enforcement databases. Enhanced due diligence applies to any politically exposed person (PEP), their relatives and close associates, with senior management approval required before acceptance of such persons. Ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening are required under the AML/CFT Act 2017 and VFSC rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: VFSC Companies Registry online name reservation and search facility (Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, https://www.vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: International Company names must be expressed in Latin script using English, French, or Bislama. If a foreign script is proposed, a transliteration into Latin characters must be provided and approved. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name, and must not imply a connection with the Government of Vanuatu or any public body.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies at the VFSC within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the grounds for acceptance and attach evidence of non-conflict, if applicable. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, further administrative appeal may be made to the Minister responsible for financial services within 21 days. A fresh name reservation application may also be filed using an alternative proposed name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this low-risk, non-resident international distribution company, provided that the International Company maintains a physical registered office at the address of its licensed registered agent in Vanuatu, where statutory notices and service of process are received. No local physical business premises are required for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annual likelihood below 10% for unannounced on-site inspections for a non-resident, low-risk International Company with no local trading premises; VFSC retains statutory inspection rights under the International Companies Act.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for IC registered agency services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992 (Cap. 222) of Vanuatu, as amended, principally ss. 5–10 (incorporation, memorandum and articles), s. 57 (registered office), and the International Companies Regulations 1992; complementary provisions of the Companies Act Cap. 191 apply only where expressly adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Companies Registry, Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (VFSC Form IC-1) accompanied by the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent of the registered agent, and notice of registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; an International Company may be formed with zero issued capital or a single subscriber share of US$1.00. No escrow account, capital deposit, or bank reference is statutorily required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Meeting of the Board of Directors of [•] International Company (registered office at the office of the Registered Agent, Port Vila, Vanuatu) resolves: (1) that the subscriber's subscription be accepted and the initial allotment of 50,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each be issued at par to the founding subscriber, fully paid against the subscribed capital recorded at incorporation; (2) that the address of the Registered Agent be adopted as the registered office, and the Registered Agent be retained for statutory compliance; (3) that [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] be appointed Secretary for the first term, each having executed a consent to act; and (4) that the Memorandum and Articles of Association, as filed, be ratified and that all officers act accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through a licensed International Company Service Provider / Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent and submit a proposed company name for availability screening. The agent files a name reservation request with the VFSC Companies Registry. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must end in 'Limited' or the suffix required for limited liability.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (1–3 alternatives)
Engagement letter with licensed registered agent
Certified passport copy of proposed shareholder/s, director/s
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Bank reference or professional reference (source of funds confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the agent submits altered or new name options at no additional governmental fee; a formal administrative review may be requested in writing to VFSC within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry, Port Vila, Vanuatu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscriber executes the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) in English or French. The documents must state the authorised share capital (typically 50,000 shares of US$1.00 each), the registered office at the registered agent's address, and confirm compliance with the International Companies Act 1992. The registered agent certifies the M&A and files the VFSC Form IC-1 with the required fees.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
VFSC Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation)
Consent of Registered Agent
Notice of registered office address in Vanuatu
Copy of name approval certificate issued at Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or deficiency letter, the registered agent amends the relevant clause or schedules the missing exhibit and re-files within 5 business days; no penalty applies on first re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – Companies Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval by the Registrar, VFSC issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company name, incorporation date, and unique company number. The company is validly formed as a body corporate with limited liability from the date certified. The certificate and certified copies of the M&A are returned to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: VFSC internal approval memo
Proof of payment of incorporation fee (US$1,000)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains typographical or date errors, the registered agent files a written request for rectification with the Registry; corrected certificates are re-issued within 3 business days at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Registered Office Adoption, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Company Secretary, and the VFSC-licensed Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 14 days of certificate issuance, the sole or lead director convenes the first board meeting (or passes a unanimous written resolution) adopting the pro-forma resolution: allotment and issue of shares, adoption of the registered office at the registered agent's Port Vila address, appointment of the director and secretary, adoption of the corporate seal, and authorisation of bank account opening and banking signatories.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set out above)
Consent to act as director (signed)
Consent to act as secretary (if appointed)
Consent to act as registered agent (filed at Step 2)
Board minutes or unanimous written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If officer consents are missing or defective, the board passes a supplementary resolution appointing qualified officers and the registered agent files amended consents with VFSC within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance and Annual Liability Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission and the Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent opens the statutory registers (register of members, register of directors, register of charges, and register of shares), files the notice of registered office and any officer changes, and calculates the annual government fee calendar. Under s. 60 of the International Companies Act 1992, the annual license fee must be paid before each anniversary of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Register of members and shareholders ledger
Register of directors and secretary
Registered office and agent confirmation letter
Calendar of annual renewal deadlines and fee schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If annual fees are not received before the anniversary, the registered agent files a late renewal within 30 days and pays the statutory late penalty; VFSC maintains a 3-month grace period for reinstatement before strike-off.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority (VIPA) and the Department of Industry, Ministry of Trade, Tourism, Industry and Investment —, identified for informational completeness; no Vanuatu industrial operating license applies because an International Company is prohibited from carrying on domestic trade or physical manufacturing inside Vanuatu under s. 5 of the International Companies Act 1992.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for the Vanuatu International Company; the ISIC 3240 compression-molding activity must be performed in a third-country facility licensed under the host jurisdiction's manufacturing law (e.g., a food-grade silicone molding plant subject to local municipal occupancy and production permits). If a VU resident place of business is ever proposed, conversion to an exempted or local company would first be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change, Republic of Vanuatu, operating under the Environmental Protection Act [Cap. 283] and the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration only (no full EIA report required): compression molding of food-grade silicone presents no Schedule 1 trigger under the EIA Regulations; the applicant must file a low-risk environmental registration and waste declaration if manufacturing is ever located in Vanuatu, which is atypical for an International Company.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No Vanuatu-specific numeric emission limits exist for silicone molding; DEPC applies World Health Organization and International Finance Corporation guidelines by default: process wastewater pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L; no VOC abatement required for non-solvent compression molding; cured silicone scrap must be disposed of through a DEPC-approved waste contractor with recycling recovery where commercially viable; no ozone-depleting substances permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If any physical production premise is established in Vanuatu (rare for an IC): (1) Fire Safety Certificate from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Services (VFES) covering sprinkler adequacy, egress, and emergency lighting; (2) structural load inspection and building permit from the relevant municipal authority; (3) workplace safety clearance from the Vanuatu Department of Labour under the Occupational Health and Safety Act No. 3 of 2017, including the submission of a risk assessment for thermoplastic/elastomer molding equipment; and (4) contractor waste-handling verification by DEPC. These clearances are non-mandatory for the standard offshore IC structure operating exclusively outside Vanuatu.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC), Department of Customs and Inland Revenue, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; official portal https://customs.gov.vu (ASYCUDA World single-window for customs). International Company incorporation and annual government fee compliance are administered by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) via its online e-filing portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Vanuatu levies no income tax, so no statutory income TIN is issued to International Companies. An International Company engaged in manufacturing and export obtains VAT identification exclusively by filing VAT Registration Form VAT-01 with the VRC once annual taxable turnover reaches or exceeds VUV 10,000,000 (or voluntarily when below the threshold). The supporting bundle comprises the printed or notarised Certificate of Incorporation, VFSC register extract confirming the registered agent and registered office, local registered agent consent, description of taxable activities and projected turnover, bank account or payment-rail details, and governing company documents. Goods export clearance additionally requires enrolment in ASYCUDA World as an exporter to obtain the Customs Exporter Code. All VFSC annual fees are settled online; no income-tax registration, tax clearance, or capital-import certificate is required for a standard offshore IC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid entity-classification election exists in Vanuatu law. An International Company may apply under section 67 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222] for deregistration or conversion to a domestic local company, which then falls within the ordinary Vanuatu VAT net but remains outside any income tax. For VAT, a person whose taxable turnover is below the statutory threshold may elect voluntary registration under section 6 of the Value Added Tax Act No. 12 of 1998. Export zero-rating requires the supplier to obtain Commissioner approval where the mandatory 28-day export window cannot be met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration applies when annual taxable turnover from taxable supplies made in Vanuatu equals or exceeds VUV 10,000,000 (ten million Vatu); voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping mandate is in force in Vanuatu. Registered persons must issue a tax invoice, paper or electronic, containing the particulars prescribed by section 21 of the VAT Act: supplier name, VAT registration number, invoice date, description of supply, amount exclusive of VAT, VAT amount, and total consideration. Customs export declarations are processed electronically through ASYCUDA World, which serves as the sole digital clearance channel for exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the VAT Act, a supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier exports, or causes the goods to be exported, from Vanuatu within 28 days after the date of supply (or a longer period allowed by the Commissioner) and retains the required documentary proof; zero-rating also applies to certain services supplied to non-resident recipients received entirely outside Vanuatu. For silicone stress-relief fidgets, the exporter must sell and consign goods to a non-resident purchaser, ensure physical export within the statutory window, claim the zero rate on the VAT return, and support the claim with the customs, transport, and remittance evidence described below.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The VRC may reassess and claw back all zero-rated output and input VAT credits where the documentary bundle is incomplete, the 28-day export window or Commissioner-approved extension is breached, or exported goods are diverted into domestic consumption. Fraudulent export zero-rating attracts the section 60 VAT Act late-payment penalty of 25% of the tax, plus monthly interest at 2%, monetary fines of up to VUV 5,000,000, imprisonment of up to three years under the VAT Act, and parallel money-laundering liability for falsified export or remittance documentation under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 60 of 2019. Vanuatu imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark in this dossier is the evidentiary pipeline standard for bank remittance and export-proceeds substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) — statutory monetary authority and administrator of the Exchange Control Act [Cap 51]; authorizes and supervises all on-island authorized dealers (commercial banks). The Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) regulates the incorporation and ongoing licensing of International Companies and financial dealers, but does not administer FX policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu operates a managed-float VUV with unrestricted current-account convertibility and de facto unrestricted capital-account convertibility for International Companies in Good Standing under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]. Non-resident ownership is 100% permissible; non-residents may hold foreign-currency and VUV accounts at authorized dealers. Profit, dividend, interest and capital repatriation require only administrative due diligence (board resolution, financial statements or tax-exemption certificate, VFSC good-standing certificate, annual fee payment) and statistical reporting to RBV via the bank; no exchange-control approval, quota, or onshore withholding tax applies to an exempt IC. Practical hurdles: correspondent-bank de-risking of small-island offshore jurisdictions, shallow onshore VUV money and FX markets, and reliance on USD/AUD as de facto settlement currencies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender ratio, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no obligation to convert export receipts into VUV. Exporters may retain foreign currency in external accounts or in on-island foreign-currency accounts at authorized dealers. Only balance-of-payments statistical reporting (Monthly International Transactions Reporting) through the dealing bank is mandatory. Recommended treasury policy: hold USD proceeds in the USD operating account and convert to VUV only for local operating spend to minimize bid-ask costs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — multi-currency (USD/AUD/VUV) with SWIFT correspondent access

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Vanuatu Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — USD-denominated trade settlement and regional clearing hub
Capital Escrow Account — share-capital and intercompany loan flows
Operational Account — local VUV payroll, utilities and government-facing transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low. Vanuatu has no dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licensing track; non-bank payment services fall under the Banking Act [Cap 62] or the Financial Dealers Act [Cap 70], both requiring a VFSC/RBV authorization that most offshore digital EMIs do not hold. Global EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex) generally decline Vanuatu-domiciled International Companies due to jurisdiction risk and the absence of on-island partner coverage. A VU IC may lawfully use an offshore EMI as a collection-only gateway for platform payouts, but proceeds must be swept periodically through an authorized dealing bank (ANZ/BSP) to satisfy Exchange Control Act [Cap 51] reporting and to preserve the on-island transactional audit trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule mandates every director to appear physically in Port Vila, but bank onboarding policy for International Companies requires at least one authorized signatory or the VFSC-licensed registered agent to complete a verification interview. Acceptable options: (i) physical branch visit; (ii) notarized and apostilled corporate pack delivered through the registered agent; (iii) video KYC interview at the bank's discretion for low-risk standard manufacturing entities. The low-risk silicone fidget manufacturing scope should not trigger forced physical attendance provided UBO documentation is complete and source of funds is transparent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO veil — nominee shareholder arrangement or historical bearer-share issuance of the International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of members; declaration of trust and nominee acknowledgment; cancelled bearer-share instrument or statutory confirmation from the register; passport and proof-of-address of all ultimate beneficial owners; VFSC-licensed registered agent compliance certificate; current good-standing certificate from the Vanuatu International Companies Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch — high-volume, low-ticket e-commerce sales recorded under Platform_Pay without an evidentiary trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12 months of platform payout statements (Stripe, PayPal, Shopify Payments); merchant agreements with platform providers; sales orders and fulfillment records for silicone fidget products; customs export/import declarations; logistics bills of lading; supplier purchase invoices; internal reconciliation of gross receipts versus bank credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Interjurisdictional cash-flow mismatch — inbound equity from a parent or shareholder domiciled in a high-risk or sanctioned-list jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shareholders' resolution and board minutes authorizing the capital injection; tax-exemption certificate under the International Companies Act; inbound SWIFT MT103 with explicit purpose code 'Share Capital Subscription'; source-of-wealth statement with third-party accountant endorsement; corporate organizational chart identifying immediate and ultimate parent entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Generic or inconsistent payment purpose codes on inbound FX and outbound disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured invoice and purchase-order set referencing ISIC 3240; proforma invoices from food-grade silicone masterbatch and mold suppliers; customs entries; a standard SWIFT MT103 instruction sheet with BPM6-aligned purpose codes (e.g., trade in goods, share capital, business services); internal treasury policy with delegated signature authority and sample board approval minutes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 (Customer Transfer) from the parent/shareholder's bank to the VU IC's USD or AUD operational account at ANZ or BSP. The beneficiary bank quotes its RBV authorized-dealer code for balance-of-payments statistics. Use BPM6 purpose code 'Share capital' (mapped from 6110/6113) with narrative 'Equity injection into International Company under International Companies Act Cap 222'. Prior RBV approval is not required; funds normally credit within one to two business days. For injections exceeding USD 100,000, the bank may require the board resolution, updated UBO declaration, and proof that no VFIPA Foreign Investment Certificate is required for the purely offshore export scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 for inventory, logistics, SaaS platform fees and supplier payments. Secondary rail: irrevocable Sight Documentary Letter of Credit issued by ANZ or BSP for large raw-material imports such as food-grade silicone masterbatch, molds and tooling. The authorized dealer debits the USD or VUV account and applies the prevailing RBV mid-market rate for FX conversion with a two-day value date. Platform payouts should be collected through an external supported-market account (US or HK) and swept weekly via SWIFT MT103 to the Vanuatu operational account to avoid FX concentration; settlement currencies are USD (primary), AUD (regional suppliers), and EUR (EU platform payouts).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore spot FX contracts in VUV/USD/AUD executed through RBV-authorized dealers
Deliverable USD/AUD vanilla forward contracts (maximum tenor 12 months) held at ANZ or BSP against documented trade payables or receivables
Offshore USD/VUV non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) concluded with regulated international counterparties under an ISDA master agreement, subject to an underlying trade-exposure test
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR/AUD) for intercompany loan servicing or capital-expenditure hedging, with board approval and RBV statistical reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal Declaration and Payment of International Company Annual Government Fee (confirmation of members, directors, registered office, registered agent, and beneficial ownership records on file with the licensed agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - International Companies Registry, submitted through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation each year; VFSC administration generally applies a one-month grace period after the due date before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee; if the fee remains unpaid more than 90 days after the due date, the International Company is administratively struck off the Register, its assets may vest in the Public Trustee, and restoration requires payment of arrears, penalties, and restoration fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit and Updated Corporate Records (physical or electronic audit of the register of members, directors, charges, minutes, and beneficial ownership register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing with a government authority; records must be held at the Vanuatu registered office and produced to VFSC or law enforcement on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation and in any event before the annual renewal declaration is submitted to the VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current statutory registers is an offence under the International Companies Act; VFSC may impose a fine of up to VUV 100,000 (approximately USD 880), and the International Company will be ineligible for a Certificate of Good Standing until the register audit is completed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: No Separate Annual Tax Filing Required (International Company is exempt from national income tax and has no statutory requirement to file corporate tax returns in Vanuatu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Revenue and Customs Authority; statutory exemption confirmed by the VFSC-registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not applicable; no annual Vanuatu tax return is due for a non-resident-carrying International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No tax delinquency arises; if domestic Vanuatu business is conducted without the required local licence, the company may be penalized under the Vanuatu International Companies (Amendment) Act, including revocation of exempt status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a Vanuatu International Company that is not conducting business in Vanuatu and is not licensed as a financial institution, bank, insurance company, or securities dealer. A voluntary audit may be required by shareholder resolution, lender covenant, court order, or VFSC direction in respect of licensed financial business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Vanuatu International Companies Act does not prescribe a statutory accounting framework for International Companies. Where financial statements are prepared voluntarily, they are commonly prepared in accordance with IFRS or US GAAP; Vanuatu domestic accounting standards do not apply to International Companies without local activity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vanuatu does not require a separate annual UBO filing with VFSC. The licensed registered agent must collect and verify beneficial ownership information at incorporation, refresh that information upon any share transfer, and maintain a current beneficial ownership register at the registered office. The annual renewal declaration serves as the annual confirmation that the members, directors and beneficial ownership register remain accurate as at the filing date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 900 per annum for licensed Vanuatu registered agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 per engagement for a voluntary IFRS audit of a small non-listed International Company; no statutory audit fee applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax; a Vanuatu International Company is statutorily exempt from all Vanuatu income tax and capital gains tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate under the International Companies Act total exemption regime. A Vanuatu International Company is exempt from corporate income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty on business instruments, and currency control restrictions. The only periodic charge is the VFSC annual reconciliation fee and registered agent fee; no VAT/GST registration is required for offshore business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Vanuatu International Company Annual Return / Annual Declaration, lodged electronically through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) online International Companies Registry portal (www.vfsc.vu). No corporate income tax return is filed because no corporate income tax exists.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, anniversary-based; there are no quarterly corporate income tax installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return is due within two (2) months after the anniversary date of incorporation. No fiscal-year-end income tax filing deadline applies because the entity is tax exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A — Company Name, Registration Number and Type
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company, VFSC registration number, and confirmation that the entity is incorporated as an International Company under the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact registered name; no Vanuatu taxpayer identification number is required. Non-resident ownership or director residence does not alter this registration field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B — Registered Office and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and the name, license number and contact details of the licensed VFSC registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office must be maintained in Vanuatu by a licensed agent. Non-resident directors cannot substitute a foreign address; failure to maintain the local registered office is a ground for strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C — Directors and Company Secretary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationality, residential addresses, passport or identity document numbers, and dates of appointment for all directors and the secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Vanuatu does not require directors to be resident. Non-resident individuals should provide passport pages and proof of residential address sufficient for VFSC AML customer due diligence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D — Shareholders and Beneficial Ownership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full details of registered shareholders, share classes, issued capital, and ultimate beneficial owners of the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident sole beneficial ownership is expressly permitted. The VFSC requires beneficial ownership data to be captured and updated within 14 days of any change; nominee arrangements must be supported by written declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E — Economic Substance and Activities Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming whether the International Company is carrying on or receiving income from any relevant activity for economic substance purposes, including banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing, leasing, headquarters, distribution, service centre activity, or a pure equity holding function.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned International Company engaged in worldwide manufacturing, branding, or distribution of silicone stress-relief fidgets must disclose those facts accurately and maintain evidence of income-generating activity if any relevant activity threshold is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the registered agent and directors that the International Company has complied with the International Companies Act, AML obligations, and any applicable economic substance requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors must personally verify the contents before electronic authentication. False certification creates personal criminal exposure irrespective of offshore residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of the annual return or non-payment of the VFSC annual reconciliation fee triggers late-payment penalties, administrative fines, and, after continued default, automatic strike-off and dissolution of the International Company. Knowingly submitting a false declaration is an offence subject to substantial fines and imprisonment under the International Companies Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Vanuatu imposes no statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No tax treaty relief is required in Vanuatu because the domestic statutory withholding rate is 0%. Vanuatu maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement with major economies; it has signed limited Tax Information Exchange Agreements with certain jurisdictions, which do not provide dividend WHT reductions. To evidence exempt status for foreign bank or foreign tax credit purposes, the International Company may obtain a Certificate of Tax Exemption or Tax Residency Certificate from the Vanuatu Department of Finance and Treasury through its licensed agent, supported by a VFSC certificate of good standing and an economic substance declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax in Vanuatu on outbound IP royalties and debt interest is 0%. Absent comprehensive tax treaties, no conventional treaty reduction applies. Recipient jurisdictions may impose their own source-based or domestic income tax on royalty and interest income, and the Vanuatu entity should maintain contemporaneous beneficial ownership and substance evidence to support any foreign treaty claim.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Vanuatu has no domestic transfer pricing legislation and therefore prescribes no VUV threshold for Local File or Master File documentation. A Vanuatu International Company is not obligated under local law to prepare transfer pricing documentation. However, if the entity transacts with group affiliates in jurisdictions applying OECD transfer pricing rules, the foreign tax authority may require the Vanuatu entity to provide an OECD-compliant analysis and benchmark study, especially where intercompany manufacturing, distribution, or royalty flows exceed the foreign jurisdiction's reporting threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu's International Companies (Economic Substance) Act applies to International Companies undertaking relevant activities. Relevant activities include banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, banking and financing, leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centres, and pure equity holding. Manufacturing compression molding of food-grade silicone tactile fidget toys is not itself a listed relevant activity, but if the vanuatu entity receives revenue as a distribution centre, service centre, or regional headquarters for the brand, it must maintain physical presence, locally resident directors and staff, adequate premises, and annual VFSC economic substance reporting. A shell International Company without those substance indicators is immediately vulnerable to regulatory sanction and foreign anti-abuse recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Tax Exemption Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Vanuatu International Company as the passive invoice-issuing party for global silicone stress-relief fidget sales while all actual manufacturing, sales negotiation, logistics, and decision-making take place in China, the United States, or Europe, and no substantive activity occurs in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu: deregistration, compulsory strike-off, and fines under the International Companies Act. Foreign jurisdictions: recharacterization of the International Company as a sham, retroactive denial of tax exemption, imposition of corporate income tax on the full global profit, withholding tax assessments, and civil penalties up to 100% or more of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for fraudulent trading and forced civil restitution of diverted profits. Courts in recipient jurisdictions may issue travel bans, asset freezes, and international arrest warrants; prolonged criminal tax evasion charges may result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a VFSC annual declaration that no relevant activity exists when the International Company in fact earns active income from cross-border distribution, service contracting, or regional headquarters functions connected to the silicone fidget brand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu economic substance penalties include substantial monetary fines, daily default penalties for continuing non-compliance, VFSC license cancellation, and compulsory dissolution. The VFSC may also exchange information with foreign tax authorities under Vanuatu TIEAs, exposing the group to foreign reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director who signs a false economic substance declaration commits an offence under Vanuatu law and may be prosecuted personally, obtain a criminal record, face a travel ban, and be required to bear the costs of the regulatory investigation and any repatriation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT and Beneficial Ownership Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing platform-pay and Swift T/T payments from distributors without conducting proper customer due diligence, concealing undisclosed beneficial owners through nominees, accepting third-party settlement without underlying trade documents, or using the International Company bank account to launder proceeds from unauthorized fidget product sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vanuatu AML/CFT framework, offences may attract fines up to several million VUV, imprisonment of up to 15 years for money laundering, freezing orders, forfeiture of bank balances, and permanent revocation of the company's registration and bank relationship.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers and beneficial owners are personally exposed to asset confiscation, extradition proceedings, travel bans, and custodial sentences where the authorities establish knowledge or reckless disregard of suspicious payment flows.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Customs Valuation Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing finished silicone fidgets into the United States, EU, or distribution hubs at artificially depressed customs values and simultaneously recording excessive mark-ups in the Vanuatu entity while failing to substantiate an arm-length pricing methodology with a benchmark or intercompany agreement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign customs authorities may assess additional import duties, VAT/GST, anti-dumping duties, transfer pricing adjustments, interest, and penalties of 50% to 200% of the underpaid amount. Vanuatu does not tax the offshore profit, but it will not shield the group from source-country assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false customs declarations may be prosecuted for fraudulent evasion of duties in the importing country, may be banned from entering the jurisdiction, and may be ordered to personally restore any treasury benefit obtained; criminal imprisonment is possible in cases of invoicing fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Onshore Activity and False VFSC Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting domestic Vanuatu business activities such as supplying silicone fidgets to local retailers, hiring local employees, operating from a Port Vila office, or transacting with Vanuatu residents without obtaining the relevant license under the International Companies Act, or filing incorrect compliance declarations to the VFSC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offence under the International Companies Act punishable by fines, potential imprisonment of directors, revocation or refusal to renew the International Company registration, and compulsory strike-off. The VFSC may also refuse to issue any certificate of good standing needed for bank opening or tax exemption proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who knowingly permits unlicensed onshore activity is jointly and severally liable for the contracts and debts of the International Company in Vanuatu, may be disqualified from acting as a director, and may face criminal prosecution, travel restrictions, and imprisonment until trial or sentence.
